probes.input:
;; v1.3.0 — `let` in VALUE position: the minimal, independent witness for the
;; two `let` defects. TR01_workflow covers the same path inside a realistic
;; query shape; this one is small enough to read as the specification.
;;
;; Statement position is a DIFFERENT emitter path: `_emit_let` renders bindings
;; as `k =: v` and emits no `let` at all, so a statement-position repro would
;; pass without touching either defect. Confirmed by transpiling both forms.
;;
;; 1. binding form — Clojure's `name=init` is legal Clojure and rejected by YS
;;    ("let requires an even number of forms in binding vector")
;; 2. infix body — unparenthesized, YS evaluates the body as its LAST OPERAND:
;;    `(let [n 3] n + 1)` is 1, not 4. A silent wrong value, not an error, which
;;    is why it needs a probe rather than a manual check.
(def plain (let [x 1] x))
(def summed (let [x 1 y 2] (+ x y)))
(def nested (let [n 3] (let [m 4] (+ n m))))
(say plain)
(say summed)
(say nested)

expected_output.description: let in value position: name/value bindings and an infix body that YS otherwise evaluates as its last operand

probes.input:
;; v1.3.0 — a keyword-key map literal, pinned through a VALUE.
;;
;; Pins the quoted-key emission in the map-literal branch: `{:a 1}` renders its
;; key through expr(), which strips the colon, so an unquoted key makes YS
;; resolve `a` as a symbol and fail. The error wording differs between ys
;; releases, so this asserts the value, never the message.
(def m {:a 1})
(say (get m :a))

expected_output.description: keyword-key map literal renders a quoted key; lookup returns the value

probes.input:
;; v1.3.0 — a two-key map, read back by key rather than printed.
;;
;; YS maps are unordered: `say` of this map prints `{a 1, b 2}` on ys 0.2.8 and
;; `{b 2, a 1}` on 0.3.5. An exact-output probe over the printed map would
;; therefore be a version-fragile test of nothing, so this pins the key
;; rendering through lookups, where key order cannot appear.
(def m {:a 1 :b 2})
(say (get m "a"))
(say (get m :b))

expected_output.description: two-key map literal; both keys readable, asserted by lookup because YS map print order is not stable across ys versions
